back: Both parties must disclose all material facts honestly; non-disclosure lets the insurer refuse a claim or cancel the policy.
The insured must suffer a financial loss if the insured event happens.
Compensation restores the insured to the position just before the loss: no profit.
The insurer pays only if the dominant (nearest) cause of the loss is an insured risk.
After paying, the insurer takes over the insured's rights to salvage and to recover the loss from third parties.
Insurers covering the same property share a loss in proportion to the sums each insured.
Sum insured with that insurer ÷ total sum insured × loss.

front: Under-insurance with an average clause: payment?
back: Sum insured ÷ value of the property × loss.

front: Why does indemnity not apply to life assurance?
back: A life cannot be valued in money, so the agreed sum assured is paid.
